The licence is as Commons records it. Identified as this saint because: A miniature of the Menologion of Basil II (Constantinople, c. 985, Vat. gr. 1613), titled by Commons 'Theodota of Nicaea with children' and categorised both under Saints of Nicaea and under Chrysogonus and 'Menologion of Basil II - burnings'. The folder's Theodota is the mother burned in a furnace with her three children, pressed to marriage by the ruler Leucadius and sent to Nicetius of Bithynia, a contemporary of the martyr Anastasia - and 22 December keeps Anastasia with Chrysogonus and Theodota, which is the cluster this miniature belongs to. The folder's text calls her 'of the city of Cilicia' while Commons says Nicaea; the three children, the furnace and the Anastasia-Chrysogonus commemoration are the same saint in both, so the place-name in the folder's synaxarion is the looser detail and the identification stands. Commons describes it: Константинополь. 985 г. Миниатюра Минология Василия II.  Ватиканская библиотека. Рим.
